clue.text: Spread fertiliser in designer clothing

parts.note: designer goods are top-end, so designer can stand for top as in top quality
a dress is an item of clothing

explanation.surface: A gardener is spreading manure while wearing expensive labels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link: designer clothing is a top dress, a fine frock from a top label.
explanation.definitionFit: To top-dress soil is to scatter manure or compost over its surface without digging it in.

clue.text: He believes it's time to burgle

parts.note: a heist is a robbery; used here as a verb, to rob

explanation.surface: A man thinks now is the moment for a break-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has faith in a god is a believer.

clue.text: Staple food in Paraguay isn't cheap

indicators.note: in tells us one word sits inside the other

parts.note: PY is the international code for Paraguay
rice is a staple food

explanation.surface: Basic food in a South American country costs a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something expensive costs a lot of money.

clue.text: Famous art critic with Russian relations

parts.note: RUS is an abbreviation for Russian
kin are one's relations

explanation.surface: A celebrated critic has family in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: John Ruskin was the leading Victorian writer on painting and architecture.

clue.text: Possibly a private padre

explanation.surface: Perhaps an army private could be a chaplain.
explanation.definitionFit: A private soldier is one example of a member of the armed forces; a chaplain is a man who takes church services.

clue.text: Greyhound is a pampered pet

explanation.surface: A racing dog is described as spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: A greyhound runs laps round a track, so it is cryptically a dog of laps.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whimsically, a racing hound is a dog that does laps; in the usual sense, a small spoilt pet dog that sits on its owner's knee.

clue.text: He said no converts have sticking power

indicators.note: converts means changes into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man refused, and the people who changed faith show staying power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converts' looks like a noun for new believers; it is a verb rearranging HE SAID NO.
explanation.definitionFit: The property of sticking fast to a surface is grip or stickiness.

clue.text: See us in action getting bugs removed

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a deed is an action
lo is an old word meaning see or look
taken as written

explanation.surface: Watch us at work as the insects are cleared out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See us in action' tempts as an anagram, but its letters do not fit; LO is an old word for 'see!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Freed of lice; bugs here are parasitic insects rather than computer faults.

clue.text: Do urgent work to complete the course

indicators.note: to work something is to shape it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone must hurry with pressing jobs to finish a course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: To go all the way round a track or golf course is to finish it.

clue.text: Ramsey is sent out on a mission

indicators.note: sent out suggests letters dispatched and scattered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Ramsey is dispatched on an errand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent out' rearranges RAMSEY IS; the definition 'on a mission' leans on 'sent out' for its full sense of an envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy is someone dispatched on a mission to represent another.

clue.text: Talk about the Italian home

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to chat is to talk
le is an Italian word for 'the' (feminine plural)

explanation.surface: People are discussing an Italian house.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss-style wooden house or holiday lodge is a kind of dwelling.

clue.text: Precise remedy

explanation.surface: An exact cure is being sought.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and particular; also, as a noun, a medicine targeted at one particular disease.

clue.text: Initially false?

parts.note: a prefix put at the start of a word that means sham or not genuine, so it is literally false at the beginning

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether something was untrue at first.
explanation.definitionFit: As a prefix it marks something as sham, coming at the start of the word it falsifies.

clue.text: Aspiring pop group of lifelong abstainers

explanation.surface: An ambitious band is made up of people who have never touched a drop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. The Band of Hope is a British temperance society for children, founded in 1847.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whimsically, a musical group with aspirations; in fact a Victorian temperance society whose children pledged never to drink alcohol.

clue.text: Hasty advice to dilatory chess player?

definitions.text: Hasty advice to dilatory chess player?

parts.words: Hasty advice to dilatory chess player?
parts.note: a phrase urging someone to hurry, read literally as telling a slow chess player to make his next play

explanation.surface: Someone impatiently urges a slow chess opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hurry up, and a chess player who stalls has literally to make his next play.

clue.text: Cumbersome word in use for foreseeable future

parts.note: a cumbersome word is a long one
a term is a word in use for something

explanation.surface: An unwieldy word will be used for years to come.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-range planning covers an extended period ahead.

clue.text: Average level of attainment

explanation.surface: An ordinary result is described as a mark of achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal or typical; also, a required level of quality or achievement.

clue.text: Intrepid fellow without hearing aid

parts.note: the ear is the organ that aids hearing, so having none is to be without ears

explanation.surface: A brave man manages with no hearing device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing aid' is not a deaf aid here but the ear itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone daring and bold has no fright.

clue.text: Likely place to see one's fate

explanation.surface: Fortune tellers are a probable spot to learn your destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means probable; literally, tarot packs are where a fortune teller reads your future.

clue.text: Since dispatched by agreement

parts.note: as can mean since, because
sent means dispatched

explanation.surface: Something was mailed by mutual consent.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is formal approval or consent.

clue.text: Herb goes "peep!" with anger

parts.note: Bo is the name that comes before Peep in Little Bo-Peep, the nursery-rhyme shepherdess
rage is anger

explanation.surface: A herb lets out a cry in fury.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Bo-Peep is an English nursery rhyme about a shepherdess who loses her sheep: Bo is what 'goes' with Peep.
explanation.definitionFit: Borage is a blue-flowered plant used in salads and drinks.

clue.text: Pressure gives son a bit of a shock

parts.note: a shock is a thick mass of hair, and a tress is a lock of it

explanation.surface: Anxiety leaves a boy rather jolted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' looks like a jolt; it is a shock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain or tension placed on someone is a form of force bearing down.

clue.text: German with access to people of standing

parts.note: entry means access or admission

explanation.surface: A German man with permission to enter mixes with the upper classes.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-born class just below the nobility are people of high social rank.

clue.text: A little sucker

parts.note: sucker here is a gardening term for a side growth from a plant's root or stem, not a gullible person

explanation.surface: Someone is described as a small fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A side growth from a plant, which a gardener calls a sucker, is a branch or shoot springing off the main stem.

clue.text: The Spanish term incorporated for glass

indicators.note: incorporated means taken into the body of something, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
a name is a term for something

explanation.surface: A Spanish word has been adopted for glassware.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitreous enamel is a glassy coating fused onto metal or pottery.

clue.text: Reporting done in prison

indicators.note: in tells us one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a cage is a prison for an animal
over means finished or done

explanation.surface: A news story has been completed behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Coverage is the reporting of news events by the press.

clue.text: Unassuming verses written in Montana

indicators.note: written in means set down inside, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: MT is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Montana
odes are poems, verses

explanation.surface: Humble poems have been penned in a western US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone humble does not boast or put themselves forward.

clue.text: Hides in a shelter in ruins

indicators.note: in ruins means wrecked and broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is hiding in a wrecked refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hides' looks like a verb about hiding; it is the noun, animal skins.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanned animal skins are leather, and motorcyclists' protective suits are also called by this plural.
